title: Trim a dog's black claws with a guillotine clipper, a cut at a time, stopping each when the dot before its quick shows
instruction: A dog-paw trimming trainer stands on the bench: a silicone foreleg clamped to its stand, the paw turned sole up with its four long black claws pointing up. A guillotine nail clipper lies on a mat. Trim all four claws with the clipper: bring its ring down over the tip of a claw, square to the claw (the blade on the side away from the toe), and squeeze the handles to cut. Take off a little at a time (1 to 2 mm a cut) and look at the cut face after each cut: the claw is short enough when a small pink-grey dot shows in the middle of the black cut face. Stop cutting that claw then; cutting further cuts into the quick and the claw bleeds. The dots are at a different length in each claw. When all four claws show their dots, put the clipper back on its mat and let go of it.
context: Cutting nails is in a Core O*NET task of three occupations. 39-2021.00 Animal Caretakers (365,300 US workers): "Perform animal grooming duties, such as washing, brushing, clipping, and trimming coats, cutting nails, and cleaning ears." 31-9096.00 Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers (132,100): "Perform hygiene-related duties, such as clipping animals' claws or cleaning and polishing teeth." 29-2056.00 Veterinary Technologists and Technicians (131,400): "Bathe animals, clip nails or claws, and brush or cut animals' hair." A black claw hides its quick, so it is cut in steps: a clinic "trimmed incrementally using a conventional guillotine-style nail clipper" and "Each cut was visually inspected for the appearance of a central black dot" (Häusler and Söhnel 2026); WSU: stop when "a gray to pink oval starts to appear". The robot seats each claw's end in a 9 mm ring between claws 14 mm apart, keeps the clipper square, squeezes through the claw, judges each cut face.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Fixed: a paw trainer (as the Erler-Zimmer VET4750: a silicone foreleg on a plexiglass stand) on the left arm's side, its leg leaving the stand at (0.3, 0.16), 85 mm up, and reaching toward -y, 34 mm thick, clamped to the stand so it does not move; the paw turned sole up at y -0.024 to 0.014, its four black claws pointing up in a row at y -0.005, x 0.321, 0.307, 0.293, 0.279 (claws 1 to 4), 18 mm of each showing, the ends 115 mm up and 3.6 by 4.4 mm, the roots 5 by 6 mm. Loose: a guillotine clipper (90 g, 133.5 mm long) lying on a rubber mat (100 by 52 mm, 20 mm high) at (0.17, -0.16): two handles 32 mm apart on centres (42 mm across), the ring 9 mm across 82.5 mm ahead of the handles' middle, 4 mm thick; squeezing the handles together by q slides the blade over the ring's top face by q (each handle stops after 6 mm; each has a return spring of 20 N preload, 0.5 N/mm). The quick ends 4.5 to 8.5 mm below a claw's end at the start (in 0.5 mm steps), drawn for each claw on its own from the seed; nothing in the scene shows it until a cut face comes within 2 mm of it, when a pink-grey dot shows in the middle of the cut face.
scoring: A cut: the handles squeezed from open (the blade within 2 mm of its rest) until the blade has crossed the hole (9.5 mm); it cuts each claw whose end is in the ring's hole (within 1.57 mm of its centre, in the clipper's frame, the clipper's up axis within 15 deg of vertical) at the ring's top face, taking off what stands above it. A claw is done when its dot shows: its cut face within 2 mm of its quick and not into it. How much each cut takes is not scored. Success (1.0, held 1 s): all four claws done and the clipper back on its mat (its frame within 20 mm of its start, lying flat within 15 deg, moving under 2 cm/s) and let go (each hand's TCP 200 mm from its frame, past the fingers' reach). Partial credit at the last step: all four done and the clipper down but not yet held 1 s 0.9; else 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5 for one to four claws done. Scored 0 from then on: a claw cut to or into its quick (it bleeds), the clipper 30 mm below the table top, or the cut model not running (an error, or not stepping with the run).
reset_notes: The clipper on its mat, open; every claw at its full length, no dot or blood showing; the leg clamped to its stand; the quick's lengths by seed. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. PhysX does not cut: the claws, quick, dot and bleeding are our model; a cut claw's tip slides into the toe, its face flat. The blade is drawn only; the handles slide, not pivot; the claw's resistance is an estimate (8 N per handle while the blade is in it). The leg and paw are rigid (clamped). Sizes and the 2 mm dot zone are estimates; the quick lengths are our choice. The cue is drawn pink-grey (WSU's oval; the paper's dot is black). The paw is sole up so the cut faces face up.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 91.7 s, step 1,834)
